To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
surface modified poly(β-amino ester)-contained nanoparticles are an effective platform for pDNA gene delivery.

(i) PBAE containing particles are effective gene delivery systems; (ii) surface modification with cell-penetratin peptides improves the transfection efficiency of PBAE-containing nanoparticles; and (iii) the use of PBAE containing nanoparticles is a promising approach for the development of a non-viral gene delivery system.
surface modification with CPPs can be used to improve the delivery of plDNA from PBAE containing NP systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of an efficient and minimally toxic gene delivery system for gene therapy applications, using poly(β amino) ester containing nanoparticles (NPs) as the delivery vehicles.
the development of a novel nanoparticulate delivery system for the non-viral delivery of therapeutic DNA.
the formulation of a poly(β amino)ester (PBAE) containing polymeric nanoparticle (NP), for the delivery of pDNA to cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

this is the first study that demonstrates a significant increase in transfection efficiency for plasmid delivery by surface modification of a poly(β-amino ester)-contained nanoparticle system with a cell-penetratin peptide.

surface modification of NPs containing poly(beta-amino ester) polymers with cell penetrating peptides (CPPs), via a PEG linker, is a viable approach for enhancing the efficiency and reducing the toxicity of gene delivery vehicles.
the use of CPPs as surface modifiers for PBAE-based NP formulations can significantly improve their performance as gene delivery vectors, whilst maintaining their low cytotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the surface modification of PBAE-containing particles with CPPs via a phospholipid-PEG2000 linker is a simple and effective approach to enhance pDNA loading, cellular internalization and gene delivery.
the addition of PBAE to PLGA NPs results in an improvement in pEGFP-N1 delivery to COS-7 cells and CFBE41- cells.
the surface coating of CPPs onto NPs containing PBLG/PBAE blend is a viable strategy for the delivery of pDNA to cells.
The main takeaway from our work is that

surface modification of PBAE containing particles can reduce cytotoxic effects, increase pDNA loading and transfection efficiency and therefore improve the potential of these materials for gene therapy.
surface modification of NPs containing PEGylated polymers can significantly improve the transfection efficiency, while maintaining the biocompatibility of the system.
the use of PBAE in NP formulation is an effective way of increasing pDNA loading and transfection efficiency.
